bug_description.normalized: The staged 33-byte radio witness is delivered to a fresh OpenThread leader instance and reaches the CoAP MGMT_COMMISSIONER_GET resource `c/cg`. The request tail is `... 63 2f 63 67 ff 0d ff 20 20 20 20 20 20`: after the CoAP payload marker, the MeshCoP payload begins with TLV type `0x0d` (`kGet`) and a base length byte `0xff`. In vulnerable `Leader::HandleCommissioningGet`, the code reads only the 2-byte base `MeshCoP::Tlv` header, checks `tlv.GetType() == kGet`, and then executes `length = tlv.GetLength()`, so the extended-TLV sentinel `0xff` is misinterpreted as a literal selector count `255`. The next `aMessage.Read(offset + sizeof(MeshCoP::Tlv), length, tlvs)` requests 255 bytes into stack `uint8_t tlvs[254]`, but only six bytes remain after the base header in the saved witness. `Message::Read` truncates the copy to those six bytes and returns that byte count, but the caller ignores the return value, so `length` stays 255 while only six bytes are materialized. `SendCommissioningGetResponse` later takes the non-empty-selector branch and iterates `index < aLength`, comparing `cur->GetType()` against `aTlvs[index]` for 255 iterations. On iteration `index == 254`, that comparison reads one byte past the 254-byte stack buffer `tlvs`, matching the reproduced AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-overflow READ at `network_data_leader_ftd.cpp:351`. The fix replaces this ad-hoc parsing with `Tlv::GetValueOffset(...)`, which correctly handles extended TLVs and avoids the stack copy.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled MeshCoP TLV header inside the `/c/cg` commissioning-get payload.
source.value_from: The staged 33-byte `poc` has sha256 `53ad7248bd8059c30ea2c3185d6f0ae41dfe0cac23b16e62a4f70f737b6690f0` and ends with bytes `63 2f 63 67 ff 0d ff 20 20 20 20 20 20`. After CoAP option parsing matches URI path `c/cg`, the request payload begins with MeshCoP bytes `0x0d 0xff`, so this read copies a `Get` TLV header whose raw base length byte is `0xff`.
source.note: This is the first bug-relevant project read after CoAP has admitted and routed the request to the commissioning-get handler.

tainted_value_origin.description: The raw base-length byte from the attacker-controlled MeshCoP header; for the saved witness it is `0xff`, which the vulnerable code later treats as selector count 255.
tainted_value_origin.note: In `ot::Tlv`, a base length byte of `0xff` marks an extended TLV rather than a literal one-byte value length, but this path does not check that distinction.

root_cause.description: The handler trusts `MeshCoP::Tlv::GetLength()` on a potentially extended TLV and uses that raw byte as the selector count without first validating extended-format semantics or that the count fits the remaining message bytes / `tlvs[254]`.
root_cause.note: The fix replaces this ad-hoc base-header parsing with `Tlv::GetValueOffset(...)`, which understands extended TLVs, rejects the truncated witness, and avoids the stack copy.

sink.description: The selector comparison dereferences the stack buffer pointer passed from `HandleCommissioningGet`; when `index` reaches 254 under the misparsed 255-byte bound, this becomes the AddressSanitizer-reported one-byte read past `tlvs[254]`.
sink.note: AddressSanitizer reports the overflow in this comparison and identifies `tlvs` from `HandleCommissioningGet` as the overrun stack object `[48,302)` in the caller frame.

parser_admitted.description: CoAP option parsing has already reconstructed URI path `c/cg` from the request and matched it against the resource registered as `OT_URI_PATH_COMMISSIONER_GET`, so execution dispatches into `Leader::HandleCommissioningGet`.

fresh_leader_commissioning_data.description: The harness calls `otThreadBecomeLeader()` before injecting the frame, so the new leader instance seeds commissioning data. That state makes `SendCommissioningGetResponse` satisfy `data && length` and execute the selector comparison loop on the witness.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness enables Thread, becomes leader, copies the exact 33-byte witness into `frame.mPsdu`, and injects it via `otPlatRadioReceiveDone`; the leader transition also seeds default commissioning data.
CoAP parsing reconstructs URI path `c/cg` from the request options and dispatches the message to the commissioning-get resource.
The handler reads the first payload TLV as bytes `0x0d 0xff`, treats it as `MeshCoP::Tlv::kGet` with `length = 255`, and asks `Message::Read` to copy that many selector bytes into stack `tlvs[254]`.
The callee reuses the same stack buffer pointer and the misparsed `aLength = 255` as the outer selector-loop bound while leader commissioning data keeps the inner comparison reachable.
At `if (cur->GetType() == aTlvs[index])`, iteration `index == 254` reads one byte past `tlvs`, matching the reproduced AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-overflow READ.

fine_trace.note: Source. After the `/c/cg` dispatch, this copies the first two MeshCoP payload bytes into stack `tlv`. The saved witness tail begins `... ff 0d ff 20 20 20 20 20 20`, so `tlv.GetType()` becomes `kGet` and the raw base length byte becomes `0xff`.
The attacker-controlled type byte `0x0d` takes the `Get`-TLV arm. This control decision skips any further TLV scanning and enters the selector-extraction path.

Root cause. `MeshCoP::Tlv` inherits `ot::Tlv`, where a base length byte of `0xff` means an extended TLV and `GetLength()` is documented as correct only for non-extended TLVs. The witness's raw length byte `0xff` is therefore misinterpreted here as literal selector count `255`, with no `tlv.IsExtended()` check and no bound against `NetworkData::kMaxSize` or remaining message bytes.

The handler requests 255 bytes into stack `tlvs[NetworkData::kMaxSize]`, where `kMaxSize` is 254. In the staged witness only six bytes follow the 2-byte base header, so `Message::Read` truncates the copy to the remaining message bytes and returns 6, but the return value is ignored. `tlvs` therefore contains only the malformed extended-length field plus four trailing bytes while `length` still claims 255 selector bytes.

Because step 3 passed `length == 255` into callee parameter `aLength`, the non-empty-selector path iterates as if 255 selector bytes were present. The fresh leader state seeded by `SetEmptyCommissionerData()` makes `data && length` hold, so the inner commissioning-data comparison loop executes on each of those iterations.

Sink. Each inner-loop comparison dereferences `aTlvs[index]`. AddressSanitizer reports the first invalid read at stack offset 302, exactly one byte past `tlvs[254]` `[48,302)`, so the crashing iteration is `index == 254`. Since `aLength` is a `uint8_t`, reaching that iteration implies the misparsed bound is the maximal base value `255`, matching step 3 and the witness's `0xff` length byte.

format.name: OpenThread radio frame / CoAP MGMT_COMMISSIONER_GET
format.contract: The raw radio frame must parse into a CoAP request on URI `c/cg` whose MeshCoP payload begins with a `Get` TLV in extended form (base length byte `0xff`) but supplies fewer than 255 bytes after the 2-byte base header. On that path the vulnerable handler records `aLength == 255` from the base header and later indexes a 254-byte stack buffer with that bound.
